ei.title: 3번: CBT: Changing Thoughts to Change Behavior
ei.subject: 빠른독해바른독해_구문독해_2024

fullPassage: Unrealistic thinking causes people to behave in negative ways. Now, cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is being used to end this cycle. It helps people change the way they think, which leads to positive behavior. Some people, for example, are afraid of leaving their homes. They think it will cause a fatal panic attack. CBT helps them view panic attacks more positively — they're unpleasant, but they're not deadly. This kind of mental shift can improve behavior in terms of people being more willing to confront situations that cause them fear. Some patients do this through a CBT technique called exposure therapy. They are being taught to face their fears directly. A person afraid to go outside might be taken to a nearby shop. The next step could be visiting a busy supermarket. Gradually, these experiences should decrease the intensity of the person's fear.

questions.passage: Unrealistic thinking ①<u>causes</u> people to behave in negative ways. Now, cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is being used to end this cycle. It helps people change the way they think, which leads to positive behavior. Some people, for example, are afraid of ②<u>leave</u> their homes. They think it will cause a fatal panic attack. CBT helps them view panic attacks more ③<u>positively</u> — they're unpleasant, but they're not deadly. This kind of mental shift can improve behavior in terms of people being more willing to confront situations that cause them fear. Some patients do this through a CBT technique called exposure therapy. They are being taught to face their fears directly. A person afraid to go outside might be taken to a nearby shop. The next step could be visiting a busy supermarket. Gradually, these experiences should ④<u>decrease</u> the intensity of the person's fear.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① causes=유발(3인칭 단수 정상), ② leaving→leave 오류(전치사 of 뒤 동명사 필요), ③ positively=긍정적으로(부사 정상), ④ decrease=감소시키다(동사원형 정상)
det.analysis:
❌ ① causes: 'Unrealistic thinking causes' — 3인칭 단수 -s 정상
✅ ② leave: 'afraid of leave their homes' — 전치사 of 뒤 동명사 leaving 필요. 원형 leave 불가
❌ ③ positively: 'view panic attacks more positively' — 부사 정상
❌ ④ decrease: 'should decrease the intensity' — 조동사 뒤 원형 정상
det.tip: 전치사(of) + V-ing: afraid of leaving(O) / afraid of leave(X)

questions.passage: Unrealistic thinking causes people to behave in negative ways. Now, cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is being ①<u>used</u> to end this cycle. It helps people change the way they think, ②<u>which</u> leads to positive behavior. Some people, for example, are afraid of leaving their homes. They think it will cause a fatal panic attack. CBT helps them view panic attacks more positively — they're unpleasant, but they're not deadly. This kind of mental shift can improve behavior in terms of people being more ③<u>willing</u> to confront situations that cause them fear. Some patients do this through a CBT technique called exposure therapy. They are being taught to face their fears directly. A person afraid to go outside might be taken to a nearby shop. The next step could be ④<u>visit</u> a busy supermarket. Gradually, these experiences should decrease the intensity of the person's fear.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① used=사용된(수동 정상), ② which=관계대명사(정상), ③ willing=기꺼이(형용사 정상), ④ visiting→visit 오류(could be 뒤 동명사 보어 필요)
det.analysis:
❌ ① used: 'is being used to end' — 수동 진행형 정상
❌ ② which: 'which leads to positive behavior' — 관계대명사 정상
❌ ③ willing: 'more willing to confront' — be willing to 정상
✅ ④ visit: 'The next step could be visit a busy supermarket' — could be + 동명사 visiting이 보어로 필요. 원형 visit 불가
det.tip: could be + V-ing (보어): could be visiting(O) / could be visit(X)

questions.passage: Unrealistic thinking causes people to behave in negative ways. Now, cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is being used to end this cycle. It helps people change the way they think, ①<u>what</u> leads to positive behavior. Some people, for example, are afraid of leaving their homes. They think it will cause a fatal panic attack. CBT helps them view panic attacks more positively — they're unpleasant, but they're not deadly. This kind of mental shift can improve behavior in terms of people being more willing to confront situations that cause them fear. Some patients do this through a CBT technique ②<u>called</u> exposure therapy. They are being ③<u>taught</u> to face their fears directly. A person afraid to go outside might be ④<u>taken</u> to a nearby shop. The next step could be visiting a busy supermarket. Gradually, these experiences should decrease the intensity of the person's fear.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① what: 오류→정답은 which(선행사 있으면 which가 맞음), ② called=불리는(과거분사 정상), ③ taught=가르침 받는(수동 정상), ④ taken=데려가진(수동 정상)
det.analysis:
✅ ① what: '...change the way they think, what leads to...' — 선행사(앞 절)가 있으므로 which가 맞음. what은 선행사 포함 관계대명사이므로 오류
❌ ② called: 'a technique called exposure therapy' — 과거분사 수식 정상
❌ ③ taught: 'They are being taught to face' — 수동 진행형 정상
❌ ④ taken: 'might be taken to a nearby shop' — 수동태 정상
det.tip: 선행사 있으면 which, 선행사 포함하면 what. 여기서 앞 절이 선행사 → which(O), what(X)

questions.passage: Unrealistic thinking causes people to behave in ①<u>negative</u> ways. Now, cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is being used to end this cycle. It helps people change the way they think, which leads to positive behavior. Some people, for example, are afraid of leaving their homes. They think it will cause a ②<u>fatal</u> panic attack. CBT helps them view panic attacks more positively — they're unpleasant, but they're not deadly. This kind of mental shift can improve behavior in terms of people being more willing to ③<u>avoid</u> situations that cause them fear. Some patients do this through a CBT technique called exposure therapy. They are being taught to face their fears ④<u>directly</u>. A person afraid to go outside might be taken to a nearby shop. The next step could be visiting a busy supermarket. Gradually, these experiences should decrease the intensity of the person's fear.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① negative=부정적(적절), ② fatal=치명적(적절), ③ confront→avoid 오류(CBT는 직면을 도움, 회피가 아님), ④ directly=직접적으로(적절)
det.analysis:
❌ ① negative — 원문 일치. 비현실적 사고가 부정적 행동 유발
❌ ② fatal — 원문 일치. 치명적 공황발작이라 여김
✅ ③ avoid — 원문은 confront(직면하다). CBT가 두려운 상황에 기꺼이 직면하게 한다는 맥락에서 avoid(피하다)는 의미 반전
❌ ④ directly — 원문 일치. 두려움에 직접 맞섬
det.tip: more willing to confront(직면) → avoid(피하다)로 바꾸면 CBT 효과에 반함

questions.passage: Unrealistic thinking causes people to behave in negative ways. Now, cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is being used to end this ②<u>cycle</u>. It helps people change the way they think, which leads to ③<u>positive</u> behavior. Some people, for example, are afraid of leaving their homes. They think it will cause a fatal panic attack. CBT helps them view panic attacks more positively — they're unpleasant, but they're not deadly. This kind of mental shift can ④<u>improve</u> behavior in terms of people being more willing to confront situations that cause them fear. Some patients do this through a CBT technique called exposure therapy. They are being taught to face their fears directly. A person afraid to go outside might be taken to a nearby shop. The next step could be visiting a busy supermarket. Gradually, these experiences should ①<u>intensify</u> the intensity of the person's fear.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① cycle=순환(적절), ② positive=긍정적(적절), ③ improve=개선(적절), ④ decrease→intensify 오류(두려움 강도를 줄이는 것이지 강화하는 것이 아님)
det.analysis:
❌ ④ cycle — 원문 일치. 악순환을 끝냄
❌ ② positive — 원문 일치. 긍정적 행동으로 이어짐
❌ ③ improve — 원문 일치. 행동 개선
✅ ① intensify — 원문은 decrease(감소시키다). 경험이 두려움의 강도를 줄여야 하는데 intensify(강화하다)는 의미 반전
det.tip: should decrease the intensity → intensify(강화)로 바꾸면 치료 효과 부정

questions.passage: Unrealistic thinking causes people to behave in negative ways. Now, cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is being used to __________. It helps people change the way they think, which leads to positive behavior. Some people, for example, are afraid of leaving their homes. They think it will cause a fatal panic attack. CBT helps them view panic attacks more positively — they're unpleasant, but they're not deadly. This kind of mental shift can improve behavior in terms of people being more willing to confront situations that cause them fear. Some patients do this through a CBT technique called exposure therapy. They are being taught to face their fears directly. A person afraid to go outside might be taken to a nearby shop. The next step could be visiting a busy supermarket. Gradually, these experiences should decrease the intensity of the person's fear.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: CBT는 이 악순환을 '끝내기 위해' 사용됨
det.analysis:
❌ ② cause a fatal panic attack: CBT의 목적에 반함
✅ ① end this cycle: CBT가 비현실적 사고의 악순환을 끝내기 위해 사용됨
❌ ③ face their fears directly: 노출 치료의 방법이지 CBT 전체 목적 아님
❌ ④ visit a nearby shop: 노출 치료의 구체적 단계이지 CBT 목적 아님
det.tip: CBT is being used to end this cycle — 악순환 종식이 CBT 목적

det.korean: 이런 종류의 '정신적 전환'이 행동을 개선할 수 있다
det.analysis:
✅ ① mental shift: 'This kind of ___ can improve behavior' — 정신적 전환이 행동 개선으로 이어짐
❌ ② panic attack: 증상이지 행동 개선의 원인이 아님
❌ ③ exposure therapy: 뒤에서 나오는 구체적 기법
❌ ④ positive behavior: 결과이지 원인이 아님
det.tip: This kind of mental shift can improve behavior — 사고 전환이 원인, 행동 개선이 결과

questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: ④ '모든 환자'가 '즉시' '완전히' — 본문에 없는 과장
det.analysis:
❌ ① 일치: 사고 변화 → 긍정적 행동
❌ ② 일치: unpleasant but not deadly
❌ ③ 일치: nearby shop → busy supermarket 순서
✅ ④ 불일치: 본문은 'Gradually, these experiences should decrease the intensity' — 점차적으로 강도만 줄어듦. '즉시 완전히'는 과장
det.tip: Gradually(점차적으로) + decrease(감소) ≠ 즉시 완전히

ch: CBT는 사고 방식의 변화를 통해 행동을 개선한다.
공황발작은 불쾌하지만 생명을 위협하지 않는다고 CBT는 본다.
노출 치료에서 환자는 가까운 가게부터 방문하기 시작한다.
CBT를 받는 모든 환자는 즉시 두려움에서 완전히 벗어난다.

questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ② 원문 일치: 치명적 공황발작을 유발할 것이라 생각함
det.analysis:
❌ ① 불일치: unrealistic thinking → negative ways (부정적 행동)
✅ ② 일치: 'They think it will cause a fatal panic attack' — 치명적 공황발작을 유발할 것이라 믿음
❌ ③ 불일치: 'a CBT technique called exposure therapy' — CBT의 한 기법
❌ ④ 불일치: 본문은 공황발작 외 다른 두려움도 다룸
det.tip: They think it will cause a fatal panic attack = 치명적 공황발작 유발 우려

ch: 집을 떠나는 것을 두려워하는 사람들은 공황발작이 치명적이라 믿는다.

questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: ③ 가장 두려운 상황부터가 아니라 가까운 가게(덜 두려운 곳)부터 시작
det.analysis:
❌ ① 일치: 'Unrealistic thinking causes people to behave in negative ways'
❌ ② 일치: 'It helps people change the way they think'
✅ ③ 불일치: nearby shop(덜 두려운 곳) → busy supermarket 순서. 가장 두려운 상황부터가 아님
❌ ④ 일치: 'Gradually, these experiences should decrease the intensity'
det.tip: nearby shop(쉬운 것) → supermarket(어려운 것) = 점진적 접근. 가장 두려운 것부터가 아님

ch: 비현실적 사고가 부정적 행동의 원인이 될 수 있다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 주제: CBT를 통한 사고-행동 변화
det.analysis:
✅ ① CBT의 사고-행동 변화: 글 전체가 CBT 원리(사고 변화 → 행동 변화)와 노출 치료 설명
❌ ② 약물 치료: 본문에 없음
❌ ③ 부작용/위험성: 본문에 없음
❌ ④ 사회적 편견: 본문에 없음
det.tip: 핵심 흐름: unrealistic thinking → CBT → change thinking → positive behavior

ch: 인지 행동 치료를 통한 사고와 행동의 변화 과정

questions.passage: Unrealistic thinking causes people to behave in negative ways. Now, cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is being used to end this cycle. It helps people change the way they think, which leads to positive behavior. Some people, for example, are afraid of leaving their homes. They think it will cause a fatal panic attack. CBT helps them view panic attacks more positively — <u>they're</u> unpleasant, but they're not deadly. This kind of mental shift can improve behavior in terms of people being more willing to confront situations that cause them fear. Some patients do this through a CBT technique called exposure therapy. They are being taught to face their fears directly. A person afraid to go outside might be taken to a nearby shop. The next step could be visiting a busy supermarket. Gradually, these experiences should decrease the intensity of the person's fear.
